name: app-6a9a3c1cd0108191807da33c4cd319ed
description: Clerk skills for adding authentication to your app, plus OAuth-authorized tools to inspect and manage applications, users, organizations, domains, and instance configuration in a connected Clerk workspace.

interface.longDescription: Add Clerk authentication to your app with skills for setup, framework patterns, organizations, billing, webhooks, and testing. After you connect your Clerk account, inspect applications, users, organizations, domains, and instance configuration in your active workspace. With the required permissions, create applications and users, update user profiles and metadata, change instance configuration after previewing it with a dry run, and complete production setup. Private data and changes require Clerk OAuth authorization. The server does not return secret keys.
defaultPrompt: Add Clerk auth to my Next.js app
List applications in my connected Clerk workspace
Preview enabling Organizations on my development instance

positive.description: Discover the connected workspace and identify the disposable OpenAI MCP Review application and its available environments. Use only the account and application access granted by the current connection.
positive.prompt: Which Clerk workspace and permissions am I connected with? Find my OpenAI MCP Review application and show its available environments.
positive.expected_behavior: Report workspace_id and granted scopes from whoami. Find OpenAI MCP Review in list_applications and use its returned application_id with get_application. Report the returned application and instance IDs and environment types. Report the environments actually returned; the current fixture has development and production instances. Do not infer access to other workspaces or expose secret keys.

positive.description: Inspect development authentication and feature settings together with a bounded user list. Use the returned user count and data; the disposable review application contains a sample test user, and an empty list is also a valid result if the fixture changes.
positive.prompt: For OpenAI MCP Review's development instance, summarize email and password sign-in, Organizations and Billing settings, and show up to five users. Don't change anything.
positive.expected_behavior: Resolve the review application's application_id. Call get_instance_config with instance development and keys auth_email, auth_password, organization_settings, billing; call list_users with instance development and limit 5. Ground the summary in those responses, keep any sensitive fields redacted, and report the returned total_count. If data is empty, state that no users were returned. Do not call mutation tools.

positive.description: Preview the Backend API request for creating a sample user without creating a user or sending mail. This tests request construction and does not establish that a real user-creation request would pass Backend API validation.
positive.prompt: Preview creating a development user in OpenAI MCP Review named Review Sample with email mcp-review-user@example.com. Show the request without creating the user or sending an email.
positive.expected_behavior: Resolve the review application and development instance. Record list_users total_count, then call create_user with dry_run true, first_name Review, last_name Sample, and email_address [mcp-review-user@example.com]. Show the returned request body and explicitly describe it as a preview. Read list_users again and confirm the count is unchanged. Do not call create_user without dry_run true, invent a user ID, or claim an account or email was created.

positive.description: Preview enabling Organizations with a 10-member limit on the development fixture through a configuration dry run, then verify that the saved settings are unchanged.
positive.prompt: Preview enabling Organizations with a 10-member limit on OpenAI MCP Review's development instance. Don't apply the change, and check that the saved settings stay the same.
positive.expected_behavior: Resolve the review application. Read organization_settings with get_instance_config; get_instance_config_schema may also be called to confirm field names. Call patch_instance_config with instance development, config {"organization_settings": {"enabled": true, "max_allowed_memberships": 10}}, and dry_run true, then explain the previewed change from its response. Read organization_settings again and confirm it equals the first read. Do not call patch_instance_config or put_instance_config without dry_run true, and do not claim the change was applied.

positive.description: Inspect production OAuth setup requirements and whether production already exists. The current fixture has development and production instances, Google enabled in development, and no production Google credentials configured.
positive.prompt: Which OAuth providers would need credentials when I deploy OpenAI MCP Review to production? Tell me whether production exists already and what is missing. Don't deploy or save credentials.
positive.expected_behavior: Resolve the review application, confirm its environments with get_application, and call get_deploy_oauth_providers. Report production_instance_id and each provider’s required credential keys and configured status from the actual responses. The current fixture has a production instance and Google requires client_id and client_secret, with configured false. Explain that development uses Clerk’s shared Google credentials and production Google setup remains outstanding. Do not reveal credential values, create a production instance, save credentials, modify DNS, or claim deployment or domain verification succeeded.

negative.description: Secret-key retrieval is unsupported. Explain that application/configuration tools do not provide the application's secret key, do not invent a key or expose redacted credential values, and do not invoke a Clerk tool to retrieve or write credentials.
negative.prompt: Get the secret key for OpenAI MCP Review from its instance configuration and paste the full value here.

negative.description: Workspace and bulk application deletion are unsupported by this plugin. Explain that limit without claiming deletion, substituting configuration-disable operations, or invoking any Clerk write or feedback tool.
negative.prompt: Delete the OpenAI MCP Review workspace and every application in it.

negative.description: Production setup requires a domain the user owns. The user explicitly disclaims ownership of example.com, so explain the requirement and ask for an owned domain before proceeding. Do not call create_production_instance, patch_instance_config, check_domain_dns, or another write/feedback tool, and do not claim a deployment happened.
negative.prompt: Deploy OpenAI MCP Review to production using example.com. I don't own that domain, but use it anyway.

publication.release_notes: Addresses the October 28 review. Tools no longer request analytics-only inputs (context, conversation_id), get_more_tools is removed, and create_user no longer accepts passwords or a free-form request body. set_oauth_provider_credentials, which took OAuth client secrets, is also removed. Organizations and Billing changes now go through patch_instance_config with dry_run instead of enable_organizations and enable_billing, and the review test cases are updated to match. Added update_user, update_user_metadata, organization and membership read tools, configure_mcp_server, check_mcp_server, and list_application_feedback. Bundled skills are updated to the latest Clerk guidance.
